input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Our note-taking app, Ledgerly, needs a theme scheduler. Target users are night-shift nurses who read notes between 2am and 6am. Today the app only offers a manual light/dark toggle, and users complain about eye strain. The goal is to cut theme-related support tickets by 40% within one quarter of launch. The feature must let users set a start time and an end time, and follow the device's system theme when no schedule is set. It must respect reduce-motion and high-contrast accessibility settings. Scope limit: only two schedule slots per account. Out of scope: per-note themes, and syncing schedules across devices.
facts: only two schedule slots per account

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Our support team at Fernloop Logistics needs an internal refund-approval console. Target users are the eight finance reviewers who process refund requests each morning. Goal: reduce median approval time from six minutes to under 2 minutes. Today reviewers open three separate tabs to check an order, and the queue often backs up by noon. The tool must show the order, the refund amount, the requester's note, and a one-click approve or deny. It has to log every decision with the reviewer's name and a timestamp. Constraint: it runs only on the office VPN, never on the public internet. Scope limit: single-currency orders only. Out of scope: bulk approvals and any customer-facing emails.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Kettleworks' public REST API needs pagination on the GET /orders endpoint. The primary consumers are third-party dashboard builders who poll the endpoint every minute. Today, clients that request more than 500 records receive a timeout, and several dashboards show incomplete data. Goal: keep p95 latency under 2 seconds for pages of 100 records. The change must add cursor-based pagination and keep the existing offset parameter working for one year. Constraint: no breaking changes to the response schema. Scope limit: read-only endpoints only for this release. Out of scope: write endpoints, GraphQL, and webhooks.
facts: no breaking changes to the response schema

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Ledgerly needs usage-based billing for its team plan. Target users are small agencies with 5 to 25 seats who currently pay a flat monthly fee. Finance currently reconciles usage by hand in a spreadsheet, which takes three days each month. Goal: convert 30% of flat-fee teams to usage billing within two quarters. The feature must count stored documents nightly and show a live projected bill in the admin settings. Invoices must list usage in GB-months. Constraint: prices stay in USD only for now. Scope limit: monthly billing cycles only, no annual prepay. Out of scope: tax handling, refunds, and currency conversion.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Streakmill needs a new onboarding flow for first-time users. Target users are adults who download the app after seeing a friend's streak screenshot. The current flow has eleven screens and drops half of new users before they create their first habit. Goal: raise day-7 retention from 18% to 25%. The flow must be five screens or fewer, collect one habit and one reminder time, and skip any account creation until the user finishes. Constraint: no email verification during onboarding. Scope limit: English only in this release. Out of scope: social invites, referral codes, and importing habits from other apps.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Kettleworks' web dashboard fails keyboard navigation. Target users are screen-reader and keyboard-only users, roughly 4% of the active base. An internal audit flagged 137 distinct violations, and two enterprise buyers have made the fix a condition of renewal. Goal: reach WCAG 2.2 AA on the top ten screens. The fix must add visible focus outlines, correct landmark roles, and a skip-to-content link. Constraint: no visual redesign of the brand palette. Scope limit: the ten highest-traffic screens only. Out of scope: the mobile apps and the marketing site.
facts: no visual redesign of the brand palette

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Fernloop needs a data export for its customer portal. Target users are account owners at enterprise customers who file quarterly compliance reports. Today these customers wait on a support ticket for two days and receive a hand-cut spreadsheet. Goal: let them export a full account history in under 2 seconds for accounts with up to 50,000 events. The export must produce CSV and JSON, include a schema header, and be downloadable from a single button. Constraint: exports are generated on demand, never stored on disk. Scope limit: one account per export. Out of scope: scheduled exports, email delivery, and PDF.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Streakmill needs smarter reminder notifications. Target users are habit-trackers who currently disable notifications within the first week. Today the app fires a fixed 9pm nudge for every habit, and 41% of users turn notifications off in week one. Goal: reduce notification opt-outs by 35%. The change must send at most one reminder per habit per day, learn the user's typical completion hour, and let users snooze for a set number of days. Constraint: no SMS, push only. Scope limit: iOS and Android only. Out of scope: email digests and web push.
facts: one reminder per habit per day

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Kettleworks wants inline comments on its shared dashboards. Target users are marketing analysts who review campaign reports together. Today feedback moves through a shared spreadsheet, and analysts say they lose track of which chart a note referred to. Goal: get 60% of shared dashboards to carry at least one comment within 90 days. Users must be able to anchor a comment to a chart, reply in a thread, and resolve it. Constraint: comments live only inside the workspace, never public. Scope limit: one level of replies. Out of scope: mentions, emoji reactions, and guest commenting.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Streakmill needs an offline mode. Target users are commuters who practice habits on trains and planes with no signal. Today a failed check-in shows a red error and is silently lost, which users report as the top reason they quit the app. Goal: let users log and view the last 30 days of history with no network connection. The mode must queue check-ins locally, sync them when the connection returns, and resolve conflicts by keeping the newest check-in. Constraint: no background sync on cellular. Scope limit: check-ins only, not settings. Out of scope: offline editing of habit names and offline charts beyond 30 days.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Fernloop needs role-based access control on its customer portal. Target users are enterprise IT administrators who manage dozens of staff accounts. Support currently changes permissions by hand on the database, and last month two staff members briefly saw another client's invoices. Goal: cut permission mistakes by 50% within one quarter. The feature must ship four fixed roles, let an admin reassign a user's role in one step, and log every role change. Constraint: no custom roles in this release. Scope limit: a maximum of one role per user. Out of scope: per-field permissions and approval workflows.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Ledgerly needs full-text search across notes. Target users are researchers who keep more than 2,000 notes each. Today search only matches note titles, and researchers report scrolling for minutes to find a half-remembered paragraph. Goal: return the first page of results in under 2 seconds for the largest accounts. The search must support phrase queries, filter by tag and date, and highlight matched terms. Constraint: no external search service, all on our own servers. Scope limit: indexed text only, no OCR of images. Out of scope: saved searches and search alerts.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Tidepool's mobile app needs a per-device dark mode setting for users who review their habit history at night. Target users are signed-in iOS and Android users on personal devices. The goal is to cut theme-related support tickets by 40% in the first release cycle. The app must follow the operating system appearance by default and remember an explicit user choice across restarts. The control lives in the Settings tab only and may add no more than 3 new screens. Out of scope: custom accent colors and downloadable themes. Team administrators cannot push one theme to every device in this version.
facts: follow the operating system appearance by default

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Copperline's internal support console needs an audit log viewer so team leads can see who changed an account record and when. Target users are support team leads on desktop, not end customers. The goal is to surface any account change in under 2 seconds. The viewer must be read-only and let someone filter by agent, date range, and record type. Scope is limited to the last 90 days of events; older entries stay in cold storage. Out of scope: exporting the audit log and alerting on suspicious changes. Access is restricted to admins only.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Ridgeline's public REST API needs signed webhooks with automatic retries so integrators can trust event delivery. Target users are third-party developers building on Ridgeline. The goal is a 99.5% successful delivery rate for webhook events. Every payload must carry an HMAC signature header generated from the customer's secret. Failed deliveries retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff over 24 hours, and integrators receive a shared test secret for local testing. Scope is limited to the order and invoice event types; other event types are unchanged. Out of scope: a webhook replay dashboard and per-endpoint rate limits.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Amberwick needs self-serve partial refunds on paid invoices so finance teams can correct billing mistakes without opening a support ticket. Target users are billing administrators on annual plans. The goal is to reduce refund-related support tickets by 30% in the first quarter. A refund must never exceed the original charge and must be recorded as a credit note. Finance staff issue a refund directly from the invoice page. Scope is limited to card payments; bank transfers stay manual for now. Out of scope: automatic dunning and multi-currency refunds. Any refund over $500 requires approval from a second administrator.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Cloverbyte needs a guided setup checklist that new workspaces see after they sign up. Target users are workspace owners creating a team for the first time. The goal is to get 70% of new workspaces to invite at least one teammate within 3 days. The checklist covers naming the workspace, inviting people, and connecting one integration, and progress saves automatically between sessions. It must be dismissible and must not block the main navigation. Scope is limited to the first two weeks of a workspace's life. Out of scope: email drip campaigns and a product tour video.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Thistledown's analytics dashboard fails screen reader and color contrast checks. Target users are analysts who rely on assistive technology, including blind and low-vision staff. The goal is to reach WCAG 2.1 AA on the five most-used report pages. Every chart needs a text alternative, and every interactive control needs an accessible name. Body text must meet a 4.5 to 1 contrast ratio. Remediation notes are published alongside each release. Scope is limited to those five pages; newer beta reports wait until next quarter. Out of scope: full keyboard shortcuts and a dark-theme audit.
facts: screen reader and color contrast checks

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Amberwick needs a scheduled data export so finance teams can pull billing data on a recurring basis. Target users are finance analysts who reconcile revenue every month. The goal is to let someone schedule an export in under 3 clicks. Exports run as CSV files delivered to a configured SFTP destination, and analysts receive an email when each export finishes. The schedule supports daily or monthly runs only. Scope is limited to the invoice and payment tables, and historical data beyond 24 months is not included. Out of scope: real-time streaming and spreadsheet delivery.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Nimbusly needs a daily digest email that replaces most instant alerts for workspace members. Target users are members who opted into activity emails but not urgent pages. The goal is to cut notification volume by 50% without raising missed-mention complaints. The digest sends once each morning and respects a quiet hours window set per member. Instant notifications remain for direct mentions and approvals. Members can unsubscribe from the digest at any time. Scope is limited to email; push notifications are unchanged. Out of scope: Slack delivery and per-project digest settings.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Cloverbyte needs a multi-language interface for its web app, starting with Spanish and German. Target users are workspace members who set a preferred language other than English. The goal is to have 95% of interface strings translated for the two launch languages. All copy must come from a single translation file so translators edit one place. Dates and numbers must follow each user's locale. A language switcher appears in personal settings. Scope is limited to the web app; mobile screens are deferred. Out of scope: right-to-left languages and AI-generated translations.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Thistledown needs saved views so analysts can return to a report with the same filters and columns. Target users are analysts and team managers who build recurring reports. The goal is to let a user save a view in under 10 seconds. A saved view stores filters, column order, and sort settings, and can be shared with a team. A view has a name chosen by its creator. Scope is limited to report pages; dashboard widgets keep their current behavior. Out of scope: scheduled email delivery of saved views and cross-workspace sharing.
facts: filters, column order, and sort settings

input:
Write a PRD for this feature:

Copperline needs bulk archive and restore for customer records so support teams can clear inactive accounts from the main list. Target users are support team leads managing large account lists. The goal is to process a batch of 500 records in under 30 seconds. Archived records stay searchable and can be restored within 90 days. Archiving requires a confirmation step and never deletes data. Every archive action is written to the audit log. Scope is limited to customer records; tickets and attachments are untouched. Out of scope: automatic archiving rules and a permanent delete option.

Write a PRD for this feature:

Tidepool needs two-factor authentication enrollment for members who sign in from a new device. Target users are workspace members with access to shared habit data. The goal is to enroll 80% of active members within 30 days of launch. Enrollment must support authenticator apps and one-time recovery codes, and starts from the security settings page. The step can be skipped once but becomes required after the next sign-in. Scope is limited to TOTP; no SMS and no hardware security keys. Administrators cannot force a reset for another member in this version.
facts: authenticator apps and one-time recovery codes
